newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-SUNS GUARD KEVIN JOHNSON TO RETURN FOR 1997-98.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-SUNS GUARD KEVIN JOHNSON TO RETURN FOR 1997-98.

text.p: Phoenix point guard Kevin Johnson has had a change of heart and will return to play for the Suns in 1997-98 after previously announcing his retirement from the NBA.

Johnson and Suns president Jerry Colangelo made the announcement at a news conference Tuesday at America West Arena. The two met on May 29 when Colangelo apparently convinced Johnson to return for one more season.

The 31-year-old Johnson said at the beginning of the 1996-97 season that it would be his last. He repeated his intentions several times during the season but admitted it would be tough to walk away after 10 years.
A three-time All-Star whose career has been plagued by nagging injuries, Johnson missed 12 games last season but led the Suns with 20.1 points and 9.3 assists per game.
Johnson quarterbacked Phoenix's unusual four-guard offence to a playoff berth after the team's horrendous 0-13 start.
In post-season play he averaged 16.8 points and six assists as the Suns nearly upset the Seattle SuperSonics in the first round, losing in the maximum five games.
In his four previous years, Johnson missed a combined 109 games with hamstring, groin and calf injuries.
Johnson emerged as one of the top point guards in the NBA in his first full season with the Suns when he averaged 20.4 points and 12.2 assists in 1988-89.
Johnson, known in "KJ", and former Sun Charles Barkley led Phoenix to the NBA Finals in 1993, losing to the Chicago Bulls in six games.
